text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait MP proposes law to ban stateless people residing in Kuwait from joining police force.

- "I pledge that we would not raise any topic (at Gulf the Gulf Arab summit) that might disturb our borthers in Bahrain," Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad said. Gulf Arab leaders hold their annual summit in December in Doha. Bahrain, locked in a territorial dispute with Qatar, did not attend a Gulf Arab foreign ministers meeting in Doha on Saturday to discuss the summit's agenda.
- Kuwait to build water desalination plant during 1997/98 fiscal year, electricity and water ministry officail says.
- Kuwait to pay in December $800 million as last instalment of a $5.5 billion international loan, Central Bank says.
- Split in Kuwait Hizbollah, political sources say. Iran could not contain differences between three trends within the unofficial political grouping.
- Social affairs and labour ministry considers temporary suspension of issuing new work permits.
